title: Runway scenario fabric & sprint orchestration for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Produce a scenario-driven quarterly runway (what we will deliver, key decision gates, and sprint orchestration) that ties Hosted API feature launches with the model catalog rotation and canary windows. This ticket synthesizes stakeholder inputs, maps OKRs to milestones, and defines a lightweight execution fabric (scenarios + fallback lanes + resource hedges) teams can use to commit to the quarter.

Scope:
- Define 3 prioritized scenarios (Baseline, Surge, Degraded-Region) each with acceptance criteria, traffic assumptions, and model fallback policies.
- Produce a staged sprint orchestration plan (canary dates, model swap windows, dedicated capacity reservations) for Hosted API and the Model Catalog.
- Produce a runbook of decision gates and owner signoffs for rollouts, with clear rollback criteria tied to latency/cost/quality signals.
- Deliver a dashboard prototype (cost/latency/quality by route + model variant) for exec and on-call review.

Non-goals: full implementation of autoscaling rules (this ticket coordinates the plan and handoff to ENG), and large-scale model onboarding (handled by separate catalog onboarding tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Three scenario descriptions with traffic matrices and explicit model-fallback mappings published to Confluence.
Sprint orchestration calendar that includes canary windows, dedicated capacity commit requests, and estimated token burn per sprint.
Rollout decision gates defined and owners assigned (PM, Eng SRE, Product Ops).
Dashboard prototype link with sample queries and a cost/latency/quality snapshot for scenario Baseline.
Stakeholder alignment recorded (Slack thread or signed PRD approval).
milestones: 2026-02-18: Scenario definitions reviewed with Eng and Design
2026-03-01: Canary calendar and dedicated capacity requests submitted
2026-03-12: Dashboard prototype ready for stakeholder demo
2026-04-02: Quarter kickoff — org-wide handoff to sprint squads
decisions: Use three-scenario fabric (Baseline / Surge / Degraded-Region) instead of a single linear plan to allow parallel hedges for capacity and model quality.
Prioritize model fallbacks that favor smaller quantized variants for cost-first customers during Surge scenario.
Canary windows will be scheduled during low-traffic weekdays and include synthetic QA traffic to validate quality regressions.
Dashboard will be a Lightdash view backed by nightly ETL; production observability enhancements tracked separately in ENG tickets.
risks: Capacity requests for Dedicated may miss cloud procurement lead times, causing canary delays.
Quality regressions could be masked by batching improvements leading to false negatives in canary signals.
Cross-team alignment (SRE, Catalog, Console) may slip, requiring an extra coordination sprint.
mitigations: Submit tentative dedicated capacity reservations 3 weeks before canary windows; include contingency for burst pool usage.
Add a targeted prompt-set regression test (top 50 queries) to canary synthetic traffic to catch semantic regressions.
Schedule a weekly 30-minute sync with SRE and Catalog leads for the next 6 weeks and surface blockers in the Friday PM alignment doc.
okrs_aligned: OKR-2026-Q2-1: Reduce hosted API p99 latency by 12%
OKR-2026-Q2-2: Decrease token unit cost for top 10% routes by 8%
OKR-2026-Q2-3: Deliver 3 model catalog canaries with no critical regressions
notes: Trade-offs: the fabric approach adds upfront planning overhead but reduces late-stage rework and provides clear fallback lanes that improve reliability during surge. We intentionally keep autoscaling rule changes out of scope to avoid blocking shipping the orchestration plan. Also, we will prefer conservative capacity hedges (slightly over-provisioned) to protect SLAs in the first run.
